Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "
could you review this rehearsal archive inventory and assess whether a volunteer can use it to locate and compare recordings before catalog cleanup? the archive has twelve rehearsal recordings from 2018 through 2021, stored as WAV files on drive R-4. filenames include the date and ensemble, but not the piece. six recordings have handwritten track sheets and six have none. some sheets list take numbers, but they don't list performer names. three folders are labeled “final,” although the notes identify the recordings inside as alternate takes. two filenames have no date, but the dates appear on their track sheets. it's unclear whether dates in filenames mean session dates or file-copy dates, and there's no written link between folders and track sheets. volunteers usually search by ensemble and piece; the archive has no transcript or performer index. please say whether the supplied information supports locating and comparing recordings, and flag information that may need checking. don't turn this into a broad archive plan or treat a folder label as proof that a take is final. make the answer a numbered checklist, with evidence from the inventory before any recommendation in each item. include the inventory details in the prompt so it stands alone.", "output": "Review the rehearsal archive inventory below. Assess whether the supplied information is enough for a volunteer to locate and compare recordings, and flag information that may need checking. Keep the review focused on those tasks rather than proposing a broad archive plan. Do not treat a folder labeled “final” as proof that a recording is a final take.

Inventory:
- The archive has twelve rehearsal recordings from 2018 through 2021, stored as WAV files on drive R-4.
- Filenames include the date and ensemble, but not the piece.
- Six recordings have handwritten track sheets; six have none. Some sheets list take numbers, but they do not list performer names.
- Three folders are labeled “final,” although the notes identify the recordings inside as alternate takes.
- Two filenames have no date, but the dates appear on their track sheets.
- It is unclear whether dates in filenames indicate session dates or file-copy dates. There is no written link between folders and track sheets.
- Volunteers usually search by ensemble and piece. The archive has no transcript or performer index.

Format the review as a numbered checklist. In each item, give the relevant evidence from the inventory before any recommendation."}]
